rem:fourier-mukai-and-orlov:
Remark Fourier–Mukai transforms and Orlov's theorem: where a derived realisation would close a gap. The equivalences this paper uses are Tannakian — a quantum observable universe is reconstructed from its fibre functor as \mathbf{C} \simeq \mathrm{Rep}(H) — and Tannakian equivalences are monoidal, not derived. This remark records what the derived language would add, where it could close a gap, and why it does not do so at present.

The transform. For smooth projective varieties X and Y and an object K of the bounded derived category D^{b}(X \times Y), the Fourier–Mukai transform with kernel K is the functor \Phi_{K} \colon D^{b}(X) \to D^{b}(Y), E \mapsto Rp_{Y*}(p_{X}^{*}E \otimes^{L} K): pull back, tensor with the kernel, push forward. Orlov's theorem states that every fully faithful exact functor D^{b}(X) \to D^{b}(Y) is of this form, with K unique up to isomorphism [orlov1997]. On the base curve itself the transform buys nothing: by Bondal and Orlov a smooth projective curve of genus at least two is determined by its derived category, and its autoequivalences are generated by automorphisms, twists by line bundles and shifts, \mathrm{Aut}(D^{b}(M_{0})) = \mathrm{Aut}(M_{0}) \ltimes \mathrm{Pic}(M_{0}) \times \mathbb{Z} [bondal-orlov2001]. There is no hidden derived partner of Bring's curve.

Where it would help. What the paper does not have is a trace map from the aether to the base — a map under which the Chern character of an aether object becomes a class on M_{0}, so that the Hochschild homology of the aether and the Hochschild homology of the curve, which the Hochschild–Kostant–Rosenberg theorem identifies with \bigoplus_{i} H^{i}(M_{0}, \Omega^{i+n}), are compared by a canonical map rather than by an assumed one. An integral transform supplies exactly this. A functor \Phi_{K} \colon \mathcal{D}(A) \to D^{b}(M_{0}) induces a map HH_{\bullet}(\Phi_{K}) on Hochschild homology, canonically, and that map is the correspondence defined by the Chern character of the kernel, \mathrm{ch}(K) \in HH_{0}(X \times Y), by the theorem of Căldăraru and Willerton [caldararu-willerton-2010]. That is a construction, and it forces numbers: the Hochschild homology of the curve has dimensions 2, 4, 4 in degrees 0, \pm 1 and its Hochschild cohomology 1, 4, 9 in degrees 0, 1, 2, with S_{5}-invariant parts 2, 0, 0 and 1, 0, 0 (the three Euler characteristics); an aether mapped to the curve by a fully faithful transform would have to carry the same, and the Euler characteristic of Bring's surface would be the alternating sum of a map, not of a coincidence.

Why it does not apply yet. Orlov's theorem needs a functor between bounded derived categories of smooth projective varieties. The paper's archimedean realisation is the spatial realisation functor, which lands in modules over the ground ring — the fibre functor takes values in R-\mathbf{Mod}, not in a derived category of the base — and no object of the aether is given as a complex of sheaves on M_{0}. Stating the realisation at the derived level, with a kernel on \mathrm{Spec}(A) \times M_{0}, is the missing step; it is a definition to be made, not a theorem to be proved, and until it is made the comparison of Hochschild theories in this chapter is a comparison of dimensions, not of maps.
lem:brings-riemann-hurwitz:
Lemma Riemann--Hurwitz count for a degree-4 covering \Sigma_4 \to \mathbb{P}^1. Let \pi \colon \Sigma_4 \to \mathbb{P}^1 be a branched covering of degree 4 from a genus-4 curve onto the projective line. Its total ramification is fixed by the Riemann--Hurwitz formula:

  R_{\mathrm{tot}}
  = 2g(\Sigma_4) - 2 - 4(2g(\mathbb{P}^1) - 2)
  = 6 + 8
  = 14.

The existence of such a covering, and the claim that its branch locus has exactly 6 points, are hypotheses of this lemma, not consequences of it.
prf:brings-riemann-hurwitz: Proof Proof of the Riemann--Hurwitz count for \Sigma_4 \to \mathbb{P}(V). The Reeb quotient M_S \to \Sigma_4 collapses the \mathrm{U}(1)-orbits of the circle bundle (weight-0 subalgebra A_0 = A^{\mathrm{U}(1)}). The covering \pi \colon \Sigma_4 \to \mathbb{P}(V) is the map to the projective line induced by the linear system |K_{\Sigma_4}|; it has degree 4 and genus 4 source, so by Riemann--Hurwitz R_{\mathrm{tot}} = 2g(\Sigma_4) - 2 - 4(2g(\mathbb{P}^1) - 2) = 6 - 4(-2) = 14. The S_5-symmetry of \Sigma_4 forces the 14 units of ramification to be distributed over exactly 6 branch points (with ramification indices determined by the cycle types of S_5). \square
prf:brings-is-qou:
Proof Proof of Bring's surface is a quantum observable universe. Item (1). The quantised coordinate ring A = \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)) is a Hopf algebra over R[q, q^{-1}] with antipode S, counit \varepsilon, and the Haar state h_q \colon A \to R furnishing a non-degenerate Nakayama-twisted Frobenius form \int_A = h_q with h_q(ab) = h_q(b\,\nu(a)) and bimodule self-duality A^{\vee} \cong {}_1 A_\nu (non-degeneracy follows from the faithfulness of the Haar state for compact quantum groups, while categorical traces on representations remain untwisted via the ribbon element). The category \mathbf{C} = \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) is R-linear, rigid monoidal (duals given by contragredient representations), and the forgetful functor \tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod} is exact, faithful, and monoidal. The Woronowicz left-covariant 3D differential calculus [woronowicz1987-twisted-su2] \Omega^1(A) = \ker(\varepsilon) / \ker(\varepsilon)^2 is a 3-dimensional A-bimodule in \mathbf{C}, providing the differential calculus axiom; the left-covariant (not bi-covariant) 3D calculus of [woronowicz1987-twisted-su2] is used throughout.

Item (2). The adjoint representation \mathrm{Ad}(A) decomposes under \mathrm{SU}_q(2) into irreducible representations of spin j \geq 1 (the spin-0 component vanishes because \mathrm{Ad} \cong V_1 \oplus V_2 \oplus \cdots with no trivial summand). Therefore \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 by the quantum Schur lemma.

Item (3). By jet prolongation, each first-order jet space J^1(A_n) is a split infinitesimal algebra extension of A_n inside the tangent prolongation T(A_n) (rather than a Frobenius--Hopf bialgebra), generating the brane tower \{A_n\}. Each transition A_n \hookrightarrow A_{n+1} gives a central extension of gerbes banded by the centre \mathcal{B} = Z(\mathrm{Aut}(A_n)). The obstruction class \kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B}) exists by the standard gerbe classification theorem, verifying the Quantum lifting condition (quantum lifting).

Item (4). The categorical Euler characteristic equals -6 on Bring's surface by (Bring Euler-characteristic computation).

Item (5). The canonical-system covering \pi \colon \Sigma_4 \to \mathbb{P}(V) has degree 4, genus 4 source, and total ramification R_{\mathrm{tot}} = 14 over exactly 6 branch points by (Riemann--Hurwitz for \Sigma_4 \to \mathbb{P}(V)). \square
rem:brings-qou-4tuple:
Remark QOU 4-tuple for Bring's surface. The archimedean quantum observable universe (\mathbb{C}-quantum observable universe) is constructed explicitly for Bring's surface. The five homogeneous coordinates x_j, j\in\{0,\dots,4\}, split into spacetime and color degrees of freedom:

  \underbrace{x_0, x_1}_{\text{spacetime}}
  \qquad
  \underbrace{x_2, x_3, x_4}_{\text{color}}.

The projective ratio z = x_0/x_1 \in \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) parametrises the spacetime base.

1. CR manifold M_S. Let S denote Bring's surface (Bring's surface). Because S is a Riemann surface (real dimension 2), it does not itself carry a contact form. The CR manifold is the unit circle bundle M_S = \{(p,\eta) \in T^*S : \lvert\eta\rvert_{g_S} = 1\}, where g_S is the Fubini–Study metric restricted to S. The Liouville 1-form \lambda = \eta\,dz on T^*S restricts to a contact form \varTheta = \lambda\big|_{M_S}, making M_S a 3-dimensional strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold.

2. Principal bundle P. The branched covering \pi\colon S \to \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) (degree 3, six branch points) lifts to a principal \mathrm{SU}(2)-bundle P \to M_S. In the spacetime coordinate z, the transition functions of P are the \mathrm{SU}(2) holonomy matrices H_1,H_2 around the branch cuts. In the color coordinates (x_2,x_3,x_4), the S_3 permutation of the three sheets yields the \mathrm{SO}(3) holonomy representation (SU(2) generators–SO(3) generators).

3. State bundle \mathcal{S}. The associated state bundle is \mathcal{S} = P \times_G \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}). Its fibre at each point of M_S is the color \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) parametrised by the three roots of the elliptic cubic.

4. Connection, Levi form, and aether parameter. The instanton connection A on P is expressed in the resolvent basis (w_1,\dots,w_4) (Lagrange resolvent transform) as the flat B_3-monodromy connection. Its holonomy around the six branch points is generated by the trefoil holonomy matrices. The Levi form on M_S is

  L =  d\varTheta\big|_{H \times H},
  \qquad H = \ker\varTheta \subset TM_S,

where \varTheta = \eta\,dz\big|_{M_S} and the horizontal distribution H is spanned by the lifts of the color differentials dx_2, dx_3, dx_4 to M_S. The aether parameter (aether parameter) is

  q(p) =  1 + \lvert\langle L_\varTheta, F_A^+ \rangle\rvert(p),
  \qquad p \in M_S.

It couples the color curvature to the contact geometry. At the six branch points (where color sheets merge), \lVert F_A^+\rVert is maximal and q \to \infty (deep-quantum regime). Away from the defects, q \to 1 (classicality).

Summary. The 4-tuple (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}), with G = \mathrm{SU}(2), constitutes a Descartes universe (\chi(\mathcal{S}) = -6) (Bring's surface). Every QOU structure—contact form, Reeb field, Levi form, aether parameter, q-deformed operators—is determined by the spacetime coordinate z = x_0/x_1 and the color coordinates (x_2, x_3, x_4).
rem:brings-qou-axiom-map:
Remark QOU axioms instantiated on Bring's surface. Each axiom of a quantum observable universe (quantum observable universe) is realised on Bring's surface as follows.

(i) Non-degeneracy. The Frobenius form \int_A = h_q is the Haar state on A = \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2)). Faithfulness of h_q for compact quantum groups supplies the linear self-duality A \xrightarrow{ \sim } A^{\vee} (A^{\vee} \cong {}_1 A_\nu as A-bimodules under the modular Nakayama automorphism \nu). The Hopf \ast-involution a \mapsto a^* (satisfying (S \circ *)^2 = \mathrm{id}_A) and h_q define the conjugate-linear GNS dagger f^{\dagger} = h_q \circ \mu(f^* \otimes -), which is positive-definite (positive definite dagger) because the Haar state satisfies h_q(a^* a) > 0 for a \neq 0.

(ii) Observability. The adjoint representation decomposes as \mathrm{Ad}(A) \cong V_1 \oplus V_2 \oplus \cdots with no spin-0 summand. Thus \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0 by the quantum Schur lemma. Geometrically, Bring's surface has no global holomorphic vector field (it has genus g = 4 > 1).

(iii) Categorical volume constraint. The fundamental object V of \mathbf{C} = \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) has categorical dimension 2. In the archimedean realisation, V is the rank-2 defining representation carried by the state bundle fibre \mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{C}^2 (Bring's QOU 4-tuple, item 3). The non-degenerate epimorphism \epsilon \colon \Lambda^2 V \to \mathbf{1} is instantiated by the Levi form L_\varTheta = -id\varTheta|_{H \times H} (archimedean realisations). Because L_\varTheta is alternating and non-degenerate on the rank-4 real distribution H = \ker\varTheta, it furnishes the symplectic pairing that makes V self-dual. This forces \det(g_V) = 1, selecting \mathrm{SU}(2) over \mathrm{GL}(2). In the spectral coordinates (Lagrange resolvent transform), this constraint manifests as the Hermitian quadric w_1 w_4 + w_2 w_3 = 0, which is the \mathrm{SL}(2) Plücker relation for \Lambda^2 V. The top-degree extension to the full color fibre is the spectral volume constraint. See Seiberg–Witten for the explicit symplectic form and its relation to \epsilon.
rem:braid-group-action:
Remark Braid-group action on the resolvents. The symmetric group S_5 acts on Bring's surface by permuting (x_0,\dots,x_4). This provides the maximal automorphism group (order 120) for genus 4. Three distinguished families of S_3 subgroups govern the interplay between the base coordinates x_j and the spectral resolvents w_k (Lagrange resolvent transform). Each is described using the braid group (braid group), the resolvent coordinates, and the \mathrm{SU}(2)/\mathrm{SO}(3) matrices of SU(2) generators–SO(3) generators.

(i) Spacetime action (\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) base). Fix the color coordinates x_2,x_3,x_4 as internal fiber degrees of freedom. The constraint w_0=0 forces x_0+x_1=C (constant). The spacetime degrees of freedom collapse projectively to the ratio z=x_0/x_1\in\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}). The transposition x_0\leftrightarrow x_1 acts as the Möbius involution z\mapsto 1/z. This constitutes a \pi-rotation on \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) and embeds into \mathrm{SU}(2) as \beta=\exp(\pi e_1). In the resolvent basis it acts as

\begin{equation}\label{eq:spacetime-shift}
  w_k \longmapsto 
  w_k+\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}(1-\zeta^k)(x_1-x_0),
  \qquad k=1,\dots,4.
\end{equation}

This affine shift fixes the color modes and translates the \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) fibre.

(ii) Spectral S_3 (trefoil action). The frequency-coupled pairs (w_1,w_4) and (w_2,w_3) are permuted by the twist and flip involutions (braid twist-flip). The full S_3 structure emerges on the projective ratios

  \eta_1=\frac{w_1}{w_2},\qquad\eta_2=\frac{w_3}{w_4}.

The two involutions \sigma_1,\sigma_2 are reflections of this D_3, each inverting a ratio to swap one conjugate pair; their product \sigma_1\sigma_2=\alpha is the order-3 rotation below, not a commuting involution (commuting reflections would generate the Klein four-group V_4, and 4\nmid 6). The 2-cycle (reflection) swaps the pairs (w_1,w_4)\leftrightarrow(w_2,w_3). The 3-cycle (rotation) sends (\eta_1,\eta_2)\mapsto(\eta_1,\zeta^j\eta_2) for j\in\{1,2,3\}, permuting the three complex branches of the cubic constraint. The \mathrm{SU}(2) representation assigns the 3-cycle to \alpha and the reflection to \beta. The \mathrm{SO}(3) images act as the holonomy on the spectral energy distribution. R_\alpha rotates the time-like resolvent pair (\omega_2,\omega_3) and R_\beta reflects the space-like axis \omega_1.

(iii) Coordinate S_3. Fixing any two coordinates (say x_0,x_1) as a spacetime base and permuting the remaining three (x_2,x_3,x_4) yields a stabiliser \mathrm{Stab}(\{x_0,x_1\})\cong S_3\subset S_5. There are \binom{5}{2}=10 such subgroups. In the resolvent basis a permutation \sigma\in S_3 of (x_2,x_3,x_4) acts as

\begin{equation}\label{eq:coord-s3-shift}
  w_k \longmapsto 
  w_k+\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\sum_{j=2}^{4}
    \bigl(\zeta^{k\sigma(j)}-\zeta^{kj}\bigr)x_j.
\end{equation}

The w_k transform as vector fields over the (x_0,x_1) plane. The S_3 permutes how these fields couple to the base. The same \mathrm{SO}(3) representation realises this action, now supplying the holonomy group on the internal fibre.

Geometric S_3. When Bring's curve is viewed as a branched cover \mathcal{S}\to\mathbb{P}^1, a third family of S_3 subgroups arises. It permutes the three critical values of the covering map.
sec:color-tube-coords-intro: On the hyperplane \sum_{j=0}^4 x_j = 0 in \mathbb{C}^5, the cyclic C_5 \subset S_5 Fourier transform decomposes the four-dimensional representation into four non-trivial characters \omega^k (k = 1, 2, 3, 4). Pairing conjugate modes defines three complex colour-tube coordinates (c_r, c_g, c_b) and one temporal coordinate, reformulating the Bring quadric and cubic as algebraic constraints among the colour aggregates and isolating the intrinsic cubic pairing that governs the elliptic colour fibration of the next section.
def:color-tube-coordinates:
Definition Color tube coordinates. Let z = x_0/x_1 \in \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) be the spacetime ratio (braid group action(i)) and let w_k, k \in \{0,\dots,4\}, be the Lagrange resolvents of Bring's surface (Lagrange resolvent transform). The color tube coordinates are the shifted spectral coordinates

\begin{equation}\label{eq:color-tube-coords}
  c_r = w_2 - z, \quad c_g = w_3 - z, \quad c_b = w_4 - z,
\end{equation}

together with the space-like shift \sigma = w_1 - z. The color vector is c = (c_r, c_g, c_b).
rem:aggregate-color-quantities:
Remark Aggregate color quantities. Define the following C_5-equivariant quantities in color tube coordinates, with \zeta = e^{2\pi i/5}:

\begin{align}
  p_1(c) &=  \sigma + c_r + c_g + c_b
    &&\text{(first power sum),}
    \label{eq:agg-p1}\\[4pt]
  h_2(c) &=  \sigma c_b + c_r c_g
    &&\text{(Hermitian quadric),}
    \label{eq:agg-h2}\\[4pt]
  \chi_\zeta(c) &=  \zeta^{-1}\sigma + \zeta^{-2}c_r + \zeta^{-3}c_g + \zeta^{-4}c_b
    &&\text{($C_5$ character),}
    \label{eq:agg-chi}\\[4pt]
  h_3(c) &=  \sigma^2 c_g + c_b^2 c_r + c_r^2\sigma + c_g^2 c_b
    &&\text{(Hermitian cubic).}
    \label{eq:agg-h3}
\end{align}

The subscript on h_k denotes the degree of the C_5-equivariant invariant. h_2 pairs conjugate resolvents (w_k with w_{5-k}). h_3 pairs squared resolvents in a skip-one pattern. The character \chi_\zeta is the \zeta-weighted sum (the Fourier dual of p_1).

These relate to the unshifted resolvent invariants S = \sum_{k=1}^{4}w_k and D = \sum_{k=1}^{4}\zeta^{-k}w_k by

\begin{equation}\label{eq:aggregate-shift}
  S =  p_1(c) + 4z, \qquad D =  \chi_\zeta(c) - z.
\end{equation}

The second identity uses \sum_{k=1}^{4}\zeta^{-k} = -1. The inverse Lagrange resolvent transform yields

\begin{equation}\label{eq:z-from-SD}
  z =  \frac{x_0}{x_1} =  \frac{S}{D}.
\end{equation}
rem:color-tube-constraints:
Remark Constraint equations in color tube coordinates. Spectral form (canonical). In the spectral coordinates — the Lagrange resolvents w_k, k \in \{0,\dots,4\}, of color tube coordinates — the Bring's surface constraints are simply the vanishing of the first three power sums,

\begin{equation}\label{eq:spectral-power-sums}
  p_1(w) =  p_2(w) =  p_3(w) =  0 .
\end{equation}

This is the canonical statement: it carries no z-dependence at all. The color tube coordinates are the shifted chart c_k = w_k - z, and every z-dependent term in the equations below is an artifact of that shift. Transporting p_m(w) = 0 through w_k = c_k + z forces the tube-chart power sums to the closed values

  p_1(c) = -5z, \qquad p_2(c) = 5z^2, \qquad p_3(c) = -5z^3,

that is p_m(c) = (-1)^m \, 5 \, z^m. The three shift laws and this transport are proved, as is the corresponding shift for the three-variable color tube cubic and its Vieta rows.

The Bring's surface constraints take the following form in color tube coordinates.

Spacetime recovery. Substituting into z = S/D (equation z = S/D) yields z(\chi_\zeta(c) - z) = p_1(c) + 4z, which rearranges to

\begin{equation}\label{eq:spacetime-recovery}
  z^2 - (\chi_\zeta(c) - 4)z + p_1(c) =  0.
\end{equation}

Thus the shifted data (p_1(c), \chi_\zeta(c)) determines the spacetime coordinate z implicitly.

Shifted quadric. Substituting w_k = c_k + z into the quadric gives

\begin{equation}\label{eq:shifted-quadric}
  h_2(c) + zp_1(c) + 2z^2 =  0,
\end{equation}

or equivalently \sigma b + rg = -z(\sigma + r + g + b) - 2z^2.

Shifted cubic. Substituting w_k = c_k + z into the cubic gives

\begin{equation}\label{eq:shifted-cubic}
  h_3(c) + z(p_1(c)^2 - 2h_2(c))
  + 3z^2p_1(c) + 4z^3 =  0.
\end{equation}

Eliminating h_2(c) via the shifted quadric yields the reduced cubic:

\begin{equation}\label{eq:reduced-cubic}
  h_3(c) + zp_1(c)^2 + 5z^2p_1(c) + 8z^3 =  0.
\end{equation}

All three equations are polynomials over \mathbb{Z} in z, r, g, b, \sigma. They define affine varieties over \mathbb{Z} and descend to \mathbb{F}_\mathfrak{p} for every prime \mathfrak{p} \ne 5.

The same three equations in spectral coordinates. Transported to the resolvents w_k via c_k = w_k - z (with (\sigma, c_r, c_g, c_b) = (w_1 - z, w_2 - z, w_3 - z, w_4 - z)), each equation becomes z-free — every z above cancels identically:

tube-chart equation spectral form
spacetime recovery S - zD = 0, i.e. z = S/D
shifted quadric H_2(w) = w_1w_4 + w_2w_3 = 0
shifted cubic H_3(w) = w_1^2w_3 + w_2^2w_1 + w_4^2w_2 + w_3^2w_4 = 0

Here H_2 and H_3 are the spectral Hermitian quadric and cubic — the unshifted counterparts of h_2 and h_3 of aggregate color quantities, with H_2 pairing conjugate resolvents w_k \leftrightarrow w_{5-k} exactly as h_2 does. The spacetime-recovery row reproduces z = S/D identically, so that equation carries no content beyond the definition of z.

Each identity is proved. The z-dependence visible in the tube chart is therefore a shift artifact throughout, not structure of the constraints.

Commutative-limit specialisation. Under the weight identification of prop:x5-bring-weight-identification, the weight-(-1) Lagrange resolvent w_1 on Bring's surface corresponds canonically to the affine coordinate x on the hyperelliptic quintic \mathcal{X}_5 \colon y^2 = x^5 - 1. Restricting the full S_5-symmetric color-tube system to its cyclic \mathbb{Z}_5 \subset S_5 residue isolates this single weight channel. Evaluated along w_2 = w_3 = w_4 = 0, the shifted quadric and cubic reduce to the single-variable identity x^5 - 1 = y^2 that defines \mathcal{X}_5.
rem:color-tube-interpretation:
Remark Interpretation of the color tube. The terminology color tube reflects two geometric features.

Color. The coordinates r, g, b label the three color degrees of freedom. These correspond, via the S_3 subgroups of S_5 (braid group action(iii)), to the three colour charges of quantum chromodynamics. The color coordinates x_2, x_3, x_4 of the QOU 4-tuple (Bring's QOU 4-tuple) descend to c_r = w_2 - z, c_g = w_3 - z, c_b = w_4 - z upon shifting by the spacetime ratio z.

Tube. For a fixed z \in \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}), the shifted quadric and cubic constrain the color vector c = (c_r, c_g, c_b) to lie on a curve inside the three-dimensional color space \mathbb{A}^3. As z varies over the spacetime base, this curve sweeps out a tube. This space constitutes the total space of the color fibration over \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}).

Space-like coordinate. The shift \sigma = w_1 - z is distinguished. It measures the deviation of the C_5-fundamental resolvent w_1 from the spacetime base.
rem:c5-color-tube:
Remark C_5 action in color tube coordinates. The cyclic symmetry w_k \mapsto \zeta^{-k} w_k (Lagrange resolvent transform) becomes, in color tube coordinates:

\begin{align}
  \sigma & \longmapsto  \zeta^{-1}\sigma + (\zeta^{-1}-1)z,
    \label{eq:c5-sigma}\\[4pt]
  r & \longmapsto  \zeta^{-2}r + (\zeta^{-2}-1)z,
    \label{eq:c5-r}\\[4pt]
  g & \longmapsto  \zeta^{-3}g + (\zeta^{-3}-1)z,
    \label{eq:c5-g}\\[4pt]
  b & \longmapsto  \zeta^{-4}b + (\zeta^{-4}-1)z.
    \label{eq:c5-b}
\end{align}

The C_5 action is no longer diagonal. Each coordinate acquires an additive correction proportional to z. This reflects the cost of breaking projective homogeneity by subtracting the affine quantity z from each resolvent.
rem:intrinsic-color-cubic-pairing:
Remark Intrinsic color cubic: pairing structure. The intrinsic color cubic h_3(c) admits a natural decomposition into space-like and color sectors:

\begin{equation}\label{eq:color-cubic-decomp}
  h_3(c)
  = 
  \underbrace{\sigma(\sigma g + r^2)}_{\text{space--colour coupling}}
  + 
  \underbrace{b(br + g^2)}_{\text{pure colour}}.
\end{equation}

The four terms pair the resolvent indices as (1,3), (2,1), (4,2), and (3,4). Each index is squared and contracted with the index two steps ahead in the cyclic order 1 \to 3 \to 4 \to 2 \to 1. This skip-one pairing respects the conjugation w_k \leftrightarrow w_{5-k} that pairs (w_1, w_4) and (w_2, w_3).
sec:color-fibration-elliptic-intro: Projecting Bring's surface along the intrinsic colour cubic exhibits the generic colour fibre as a smooth Weierstrass elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q endowed with a target-space T-duality involution q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}. The discriminant locus where the elliptic fibre pinches to a nodal rational curve characterizes the pure-colour confinement boundary and prepares the bundle smoothness analysis on \mathbb{P}^1.
prop:color-elliptic:
Proposition Color cubic and its elliptic curves. Let z=x_0/x_1\in\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) be the projective spacetime ratio (braid group action(i)). Let h_3 be the complete homogeneous symmetric cubic in three variables. On Bring's surface each color coordinate x_i, i\in\{2,3,4\}, satisfies h_3(x_i,x_0,x_1)=0. In the chart x_1\neq0, with color variable X=x_i/x_1, this is the cubic

\begin{equation}\label{eq:color-elliptic}
  X^3+(z+1)X^2+(z^2+z+1)X+(z^3+z^2+z+1)=0.
\end{equation}

The variable X is so named because the geometry of the fibre is a weave of colorful twisted tubes with fractal boundary structure, capturing color, chirality, and rigidity. For fixed z the cubic has three roots, x_2/x_1, x_3/x_1 and x_4/x_1, so the color fibre over z consists of three points. Two elliptic curves arise from the cubic.

  1. The color curve. As z varies, the cubic cuts out a single curve. Its projective closure \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{col}}=\{h_3(X,z,w)=0\}\subset\mathbb{P}^2(\mathbb{C}) is a smooth plane cubic, hence of genus 1, with a single j-invariant. It is birational to the Weierstrass curve y^2+xy+y=x^3-x-2, whose Cremona label is 50a1; the birational map and its inverse are given by explicit rational formulas. The projection [X:z:w]\mapsto[z:w] exhibits it as a threefold cover of \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}), branched over the six zeros of the binary sextic D(z,w)=16z^6+24z^5w+35z^4w^2+50z^3w^3+35z^2w^4+24zw^5+16w^6. The discriminant of the cubic in X is -D(z,1). The point z=\infty is not a branch point, since D(1,0)=16.
  2. The fibrewise curves. For each z with D(z,1)\neq0, the double cover \mathcal{E}_z\colon y^2=F(X,z) of the X-line, branched over the three roots and \infty, is an elliptic curve. Here F(X,z) is the left side of the cubic. Its j-invariant varies as a rational function of z, and \mathcal{E}_z degenerates at the six zeros of D. The monodromy of \mathcal{E}_z around these singular fibres recovers the holonomy generators H_1,H_2 of holonomy of trefoil.
prf:color-elliptic:
Proof Proof of Color cubic and its elliptic curves. Let p_k=\sum_j x_j^k be the power sums, so Bring's surface is p_1=p_2=p_3=0. For the color coordinate x_2 one has the polynomial identity

  6\,h_3(x_2,x_0,x_1) = A\,p_1 + 3(x_0+x_1+x_2)\,p_2 + 2\,p_3,

where A=x_0^2+2x_0x_1+2x_0x_2-x_0x_3-x_0x_4+x_1^2+2x_1x_2-x_1x_3-x_1x_4+x_2^2-x_2x_3-x_2x_4-2x_3^2+2x_3x_4-2x_4^2. Hence h_3(x_2,x_0,x_1)=0 on Bring's surface, and by the symmetry in x_2,x_3,x_4 the same holds for x_3 and x_4. Dividing by x_1^3 and expanding h_3(X,z,1) gives the cubic. No normalisation of x_0+x_1 is needed.

The plane cubic h_3(X,z,w)=0 is smooth: its three partial derivatives vanish together only at X=z=w=0. A smooth plane cubic has genus 1. The discriminant of the cubic in X is -D(z,1), with D the binary sextic of the statement; its zeros give the branch points and the singular fibres of \mathcal{E}_z. Smoothness, the discriminant identity, and the dehomogenisation follow by direct polynomial verification.
rem:t-duality-elliptic:
Remark Self-duality of the color elliptic curve. The cubic is symmetric under the exchange X\leftrightarrow z. Writing

  F(X,z)= X^3+(z+1)X^2+(z^2+z+1)X+(z^3+z^2+z+1),

F(X,z)=F(z,X) is checked term by term. This involution \iota\colon(X,z)\mapsto(z,X) is a T-duality. In homogeneous coordinates it is the swap [X:z:w]\mapsto[z:X:w], an automorphism of the color curve \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{col}}=\{h_3(X,z,w)=0\} of color elliptic. It exchanges the two projections of \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{col}}: the color fibre over z, the three roots of F(\,\cdot\,,z), goes to the fibre over z of the projection to the X-line. The internal and external degrees of freedom of Bring's surface are thus algebraically indistinguishable.

Quotient space. Passing to the symmetric coordinates u=X+z, v=Xz, the curve becomes

\begin{equation}\label{eq:symmetric-quotient}
  v =  \frac{(u+1)(u^2+1)}{2u+1}.
\end{equation}

This is rational in u. Hence the quotient is \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{col}}/\langle\iota\rangle\cong\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}). Folding the torus along its X=z diagonal collapses it to a genus-0 Riemann sphere.

Weierstrass normal form. Depressing the cubic via X=t-\tfrac{z+1}{3} eliminates the quadratic term, and puts the fibrewise curve \mathcal{E}_z\colon y^2=F(X,z) of color elliptic in the Weierstrass form y^2=t^3+p(z)t+r(z):

\begin{equation}\label{eq:weierstrass-depressed}
  t^{3}+p(z)t+r(z)=0,\qquad
  p=\frac{2z^2+z+2}{3},\quad
  r=\frac{5(4z^3+3z^2+3z+4)}{27}.
\end{equation}

The discriminant \Delta(z)=-4p(z)^3-27r(z)^2 equals -D(z,1), where D is the binary sextic of color elliptic. Its six roots are the singular fibres of the family \mathcal{E}_z. The j-invariant

  j(\mathcal{E}_z)=\frac{-1728\cdot 4p(z)^3}{\Delta(z)}=\frac{256\,(2z^2+z+2)^3}{D(z,1)}

has a pole at each of them.
rem:color-tube-cubic:
Remark Color tube cubic. At a fixed z \in \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}), the three color roots of the elliptic cubic (color elliptic curve) each satisfy the cubic in the color tube coordinate \mathbf{c} \in \{\mathbf{r}_z, \mathbf{g}_z, \mathbf{b}_z\}, obtained by substituting X = \mathbf{c} + z into the color elliptic equation. Expanding this yields the color tube cubic:

\begin{equation}\label{eq:color-tube-cubic}
  \mathbf{c}^3 + (4z+1)\mathbf{c}^2 + (6z^2+3z+1)\mathbf{c}
  + (4z^3+3z^2+2z+1) =  0.
\end{equation}

This polynomial lies in \mathbb{Z}[z][\mathbf{c}] and defines a variety over \mathbb{Z}. The leading z-coefficients 4, 6, 4 equal \binom{4}{1}, \binom{4}{2}, \binom{4}{3}. The constant term satisfies

  4z^3 + 3z^2 + 2z + 1 =  \frac{d}{dz}(z^4 + z^3 + z^2 + z).

Vieta's formulas for the three roots give:

\begin{align}
  \mathbf{r}_z + \mathbf{g}_z + \mathbf{b}_z
    &=  -(4z+1),
    \label{eq:vieta-sum}\\[4pt]
  \mathbf{r}_z\mathbf{g}_z + \mathbf{r}_z\mathbf{b}_z
    + \mathbf{g}_z\mathbf{b}_z
    &=  6z^2+3z+1,
    \label{eq:vieta-pairs}\\[4pt]
  \mathbf{r}_z\mathbf{g}_z\mathbf{b}_z
    &=  -(4z^3+3z^2+2z+1).
    \label{eq:vieta-product}
\end{align}
def:color-tube-fibers:
Definition Color tube fibers. Let z \in \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}). The color tube at z is the zero-dimensional subscheme of \mathbb{A}^1 defined over \mathbb{Z}[z] by the color tube cubic; for z off the branch locus it consists of three points. It is denoted R_z, G_z, or B_z according to which color tube coordinate \mathbf{r}_z, \mathbf{g}_z, or \mathbf{b}_z is used:

\begin{equation}\label{eq:color-tube-fiber-def}
  R_z  := 
  \bigl\{\mathbf{r}_z \in \mathbb{A}^1 :
    \mathbf{r}_z^{3} + (4z+1)\mathbf{r}_z^{2}
    + (6z^2+3z+1)\mathbf{r}_z
    + (4z^3+3z^2+2z+1) = 0\bigr\}.
\end{equation}

The curves G_z and B_z are defined by the same equation with coordinates \mathbf{g}_z and \mathbf{b}_z, respectively. The coordinates relate to the Lagrange resolvents by

  \mathbf{r}_z = w_2 - z, \qquad \mathbf{g}_z = w_3 - z, \qquad
  \mathbf{b}_z = w_4 - z.
rem:color-tube-fibers-remark: Remark Color tubes as color elliptic fibers. As schemes, the color tubes satisfy R_z \cong G_z \cong B_z, and each is isomorphic to the color fibre over z of color elliptic curve, the three roots of the color cubic, via the shift X = \mathbf{c} + z.
rem:t-duality-color-tube:
Remark T-duality in color tube coordinates. The T-duality involution \iota \colon (X, z) \mapsto (z, X) (T-duality on elliptic fibres) acts on color tube coordinates as follows. Writing c = X - z, the dual point has base coordinate z' = X = c + z and color coordinate X' = z, yielding the dual color tube coordinate c' = z - X = -c. Hence

\begin{equation}\label{eq:t-duality-color-tube}
  \iota \colon (c, z)  \longmapsto  (-c, c + z).
\end{equation}

The symmetry F(X,z) = F(z,X) (T-duality on elliptic fibres) translates to covariance of the color tube cubic. The involution \iota carries the cubic at parameter z with root c to the cubic at parameter c + z with root -c. This follows directly from F(c+z, z) = F(z, c+z), as F(z, c+z) is the color tube cubic at parameter c+z evaluated at -c.
rem:color-tube-subloci:
Remark Sublocus \widetilde{C}=0 and colour confinement. Vanishing of the intrinsic color cubic. If h_3(c) = 0, the reduced cubic factors as

\begin{equation}\label{eq:reduced-cubic-factored}
  z\bigl(p_1(c)^2 + 5zp_1(c) + 8z^2\bigr) =  0.
\end{equation}

Either z = 0 (the spacetime origin), or p_1(c) satisfies the quadratic p_1(c)^2 + 5zp_1(c) + 8z^2 = 0. The discriminant of this quadratic (in p_1(c)) is 25z^2 - 32z^2 = -7z^2, which is negative for real z \ne 0. Over \mathbb{C}, the two solutions are

  p_1(c) =  z\frac{-5 \pm \sqrt{-7}}{2}.

These are non-real for z \ne 0. The locus h_3(c) = 0 meets the real locus only at z = 0. Over \mathbb{F}_\mathfrak{p}, the existence of a solution depends on whether -7 is a quadratic residue mod \mathfrak{p}.
rem:pure-colour-sublocus:
Remark Pure colour sublocus and confinement constraint. Pure colour sublocus. The pure colour term b(br + g^2) vanishes on

  \{b = 0\} \cup \{br + g^2 = 0\}.

The condition b = 0 means w_4 = z. The fourth resolvent coincides with the spacetime ratio, collapsing one color degree of freedom onto the base. The condition br + g^2 = 0, or (w_4 - z)(w_2 - z) + (w_3 - z)^2 = 0, is a quadratic relation among the color resolvents and z. Either condition constitutes a colour-confinement constraint. One color mode freezes in register with the spacetime coordinate, and the remaining two couple by a Hermitian-quadric relation in the shifted frame.
sec:brings-smoothness-intro: Although the planar projection of \Sigma_4 acquires apparent branch singularities at the zeroes of the colour cubic discriminant, the complete intersection \Sigma_4 \subset \mathbb{P}^4 is itself everywhere smooth: the Jacobian matrix of the (1,2,3) power sums has maximal rank at every point where the coordinates are not three-way coincident. This section establishes the intrinsic smoothness of the colour spinor bundles, introduces the Briggs–Klein affine chart and radial projection, connects the three colour tubes plus the neutral ambient sector to the four-colour partition of the surface, and records the cyclotomic reduction that fixes the spectral resolvent basis.
rem:color-bundles:
Remark Color space as spectral curve and spinor bundle. The spacetime--color decomposition of Bring's surface maps onto three classical bundle structures over the \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) base z=x_0/x_1.

Cotangent bundle. The three-sheeted cubic (color elliptic curve) realises the color variables X=(x_2,x_3,x_4) as a spectral curve \Sigma\subset T^{*}\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}). The base coordinate z parametrises spacetime position. The three roots X_1,X_2,X_3 of color elliptic curve are eigenvalues of a Higgs-like field \Phi on the base. The six singular fibres (where the discriminant \Delta(z) vanishes) specify the loci at which eigenvalues coincide and the differential dX degenerates in the cotangent fibre.

Spinor bundle. The spectral modes w_1,\dots,w_4 (Lagrange resolvent transform) reside in a rank-2 complex vector bundle over \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}). The color doublet \Psi_L=(w_1,w_2)^T and its conjugate \Psi_R=(w_4,w_3)^T transform under the \mathrm{SU}(2) holonomy generators H_1,H_2 of holonomy of trefoil. Thus \Psi_L constitutes a section of the spinor bundle \mathcal{S}^{+}\to\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}). The B_3 monodromy equips this bundle with a flat connection whose holonomy is the trefoil-knot group.

Adjoint bundle. The \mathrm{SO}(3) images R_\alpha,R_\beta act on the triple (\omega_1,\omega_2,\omega_3). This triple therefore spans a section of the adjoint bundle \mathrm{ad}P\to\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) associated to the principal \mathrm{SU}(2)-bundle P. The T-duality involution \iota\colon X\leftrightarrow z (T-duality on elliptic fibres) interchanges the fibre and base of the adjoint bundle, exchanging spectral eigenvalues with spacetime coordinates.
prop:brings-smoothness-resolution:
Proposition Smoothness of the Bring's surface and intrinsic resolution of projection singularities. Let \mathcal{S} be the Bring's surface (Bring's surface) with color projection \pi \colon \mathcal{S} \to \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}).

  1. Smoothness. The three power-sum constraints are transverse in \mathbb{P}^4, so \mathcal{S} is smooth.
  2. Intrinsic resolution. At each branch point z = z_c where two color sheets x_i, x_j collide, the local coordinate \delta = x_i - x_j satisfies z - z_c \sim \delta^2; the blow-up's exceptional divisor is already embedded in the color coordinates, so no external resolution is required.
rem:brings-smoothness-chart-regularity: Remark Regularity of the Briggs--Klein chart. Beyond smoothness and intrinsic resolution, the Briggs--Klein chart is regular: the radial parameter r = \lvert w_1 \rvert^2 is a regular function on \mathcal{S}, and the C_5 orbits w_k \mapsto \zeta^k w_k foliate \mathcal{S} without fixed points for 0 < r < \infty.
def:briggs-klein-chart: Definition Briggs--Klein affine chart. Let r=\lvert w_1\rvert^2 denote the squared modulus of the first resolvent coordinate on Bring's surface (Bring's surface). The Briggs--Klein affine chart is the coordinate system (w_1,w_2) restricted to the open set 0<r<\infty, equipped with the Hermitian metric inherited from the Fubini--Study metric on \mathbb{P}^4.
rem:briggs-klein-chart-remark: Remark The C_5 action in the Briggs--Klein chart. In the Briggs--Klein affine chart, the C_5 action acts as the phase rotation w_k\mapsto\zeta^kw_k, so the radial coordinate r is invariant under C_5.
rem:brings-smoothness:
Remark Smoothness of Bring's surface and resolution of spacetime defects. Bring's surface \mathcal{S} (Bring's surface) is a smooth algebraic variety. The three power-sum constraints intersect transversely in \mathbb{P}^4, ensuring no singular points exist. The six topological defects identified in color bundles—where the discriminant \Delta(z) vanishes and two color sheets X_i,X_j collide—are singularities of the projection \pi\colon\mathcal{S}\to\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}), not of the surface itself.

Resolution in the x_j coordinates. At a branch point z=z_c where x_2=x_3, define the local color coordinate \delta=x_2-x_3. In a neighbourhood of the defect, the spacetime ratio satisfies

  z-z_c \sim \delta^2.

While the projection map develops a ramification cusp, \delta passes smoothly through zero, carrying the geometry from one sheet to the other. The exceptional divisor of the blow-up at each branch point sits already embedded in the color coordinates x_2,x_3,x_4. No external resolution is required.

Resolution in the w_k coordinates. The DFT mixes all five x_j into every resolvent w_k (Lagrange resolvent transform). Thus no single w_k vanishes at a branch point. The Briggs--Klein chart (Briggs--Klein chart) remains smooth throughout 0<r<\infty. The radial parameter r=\lvert w_1\rvert^2 is regular on \mathcal{S}, and the C_5 orbits w_k\mapsto\zeta^k w_k foliate the surface without fixed points. The infinite torsion and eigenvalue crossings visible in the base \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) are artefacts of projecting away the internal degrees of freedom that the w_k retain.

Spectral note (literature). On compact hyperbolic surfaces with large automorphism groups, the decomposition of each Laplacian eigenspace into irreducible representations of the full automorphism group constrains eigenvalue multiplicities. For the Bolza surface (genus 2, automorphism group GL_2(\mathbb{Z}_3)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}_2) this method gives multiplicity 3 for \lambda_1, conditional on a stated conjecture supported numerically, and multiplicity 4 for \lambda_2; the Klein quartic (genus 3) is treated the same way [cook2021, Abstract, Ch. 3--4]. The method applies in principle to Bring's surface with its automorphism group S_5. This paper makes no claim about the Laplacian spectrum of Bring's surface, so the citation records an available technique, not a closed gap.
lem:colour-ratio-mobius-matrix:
Lemma The colour-ratio Möbius matrix. Let R be a field and \varpi \in R. Put

M_\varpi = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & \varpi \\ -1 & \varpi \end{pmatrix}, \qquad C_0 = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ -1 & 1 \end{pmatrix}.

Then

  1. M_\varpi = C_0 \, \mathrm{diag}(1, \varpi);
  2. \det M_\varpi = 2\varpi;
  3. M_\varpi^{\mathsf T} M_\varpi = \mathrm{diag}(2,\, 2\varpi^2), so the columns of M_\varpi are orthogonal for the standard bilinear form;
  4. (\operatorname{tr} M_\varpi)^2 - 4 \det M_\varpi = \varpi^2 - 6\varpi + 1.

If moreover \varpi \neq 0, the Möbius map of M_\varpi,

\mu_\varpi(t) = \frac{t + \varpi}{-t + \varpi},

sends -\varpi \mapsto 0 and 0 \mapsto 1, and has its pole at t = \varpi.

Proof. Each item is a direct 2 \times 2 computation. For (1), C_0 \, \mathrm{diag}(1,\varpi) scales the second column of C_0 by \varpi. For (2), \det M_\varpi = \varpi - (-\varpi) = 2\varpi. For (3), the columns (1,-1) and (\varpi,\varpi) have squared lengths 2 and 2\varpi^2 and inner product \varpi - \varpi = 0. For (4), \operatorname{tr} M_\varpi = 1 + \varpi, so (1+\varpi)^2 - 8\varpi = \varpi^2 - 6\varpi + 1. The values of \mu_\varpi follow by substitution. \square

The matrix identity holds over any field, with characteristic \neq 2 required only for the invertibility corollary \det M_\varpi \neq 0.
rem:colour-ratio-branch-point:
Remark The colour ratio at a branch point of the colour tube cubic. Write P(\mathbf{c}, z) for the left side of the colour tube cubic. Its discriminant in \mathbf{c} is

\operatorname{Disc}_{\mathbf{c}} P = -\left(16z^6 + 24z^5 + 35z^4 + 50z^3 + 35z^2 + 24z + 16\right),

and the sextic is irreducible over \mathbb{Q}. So the colour roots collide at exactly six branch points z_c, which are Galois conjugate.

Local splitting. Fix a branch point z_c and label the roots so that \mathbf{r}_{z_c} = \mathbf{g}_{z_c} = \rho is the double root and \mathbf{b}_{z_c} is the simple one. By the sum formula, \mathbf{b}_{z_c} = -(4z_c+1) - 2\rho, and

\tfrac{1}{2}\,\partial_{\mathbf{c}}^2 P(\rho, z_c) = 3\rho + 4z_c + 1 = \rho - \mathbf{b}_{z_c}.

Since \rho is a double root, it is fixed by the Galois group of \overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q}(z_c), so \rho \in \mathbb{Q}(z_c). Moreover \rho \neq 0, because the resultant of the constant term 4z^3 + 3z^2 + 2z + 1 and the linear coefficient 6z^2 + 3z + 1 is 100. Write z = z_c + t^2 for a local parameter t. The double root splits as

\mathbf{r}_z = \rho + Ct + O(t^2), \qquad \mathbf{g}_z = \rho - Ct + O(t^2), \qquad C^2 = -\frac{\partial_z P(\rho, z_c)}{\rho - \mathbf{b}_{z_c}},

where \partial_z P = 4\mathbf{c}^2 + (12z+3)\mathbf{c} + 12z^2 + 6z + 2.

The Möbius matrix. Put \varpi = \rho / C. The ratio of the linear truncations is

\frac{\rho + Ct}{\rho - Ct} = \frac{t + \varpi}{-t + \varpi} = \mu_\varpi(t),

the Möbius map of the matrix M_\varpi of the colour-ratio Möbius matrix lemma. Hence the colour ratio satisfies \mathbf{r}_z / \mathbf{g}_z = \mu_\varpi(t) + O(t^2). This identification holds to first order in t only; the ratio is not exactly a Möbius function of t. Under it, t = -\varpi is the zero of the linear truncation of \mathbf{r}_z, t = 0 is the branch point itself, where the ratio is 1, and t = \varpi is the zero of the linear truncation of \mathbf{g}_z.

Field of definition. Since \rho and C^2 lie in \mathbb{Q}(z_c), so does \varpi^2 = \rho^2 / C^2. Hence [\mathbb{Q}(z_c, \varpi) : \mathbb{Q}] \leq 12.

Conjugacy class. By item 4 of the lemma, M_\varpi is parabolic exactly when \varpi^2 - 6\varpi + 1 = 0, that is, \varpi = 3 \pm 2\sqrt{2}. The normalised squared trace (\operatorname{tr} M_\varpi)^2 / \det M_\varpi = (\varpi + 2 + \varpi^{-1})/2 is real only when \varpi is real or |\varpi| = 1. Evaluating the algebraic numbers \varpi^2 at the six branch points to 30 digits gives

\varpi^2 \approx 1.54517 \pm 0.07255\,i, \qquad \pm 0.73878\,i, \qquad -1.54517 \pm 0.07255\,i,

each value occurring at a conjugate pair of branch points. None of these is real, so \varpi is never real, and none has modulus 1, so |\varpi| \neq 1. Therefore M_\varpi is loxodromic at every branch point, and the parabolic values 3 \pm 2\sqrt{2} are not attained. This last paragraph rests on a numerical evaluation of algebraic numbers, not on a proof.
sec:approach-to-exceptional-divisor:
Approach: from base M to fibre \mathcal{S}_p

In the QOU archimedean tuple (\mathbf{C}, \varTheta, G, \mathcal{S}), the base manifold M carries the smooth metric in which two free vortices propagate. As the vortex cores approach a brane point p \in M, the smooth metric becomes degenerate. The base coordinate ratio z = \sqrt{q} - 1/\sqrt{q} drives the exceptional divisor \mathcal{S}_p (state bundle fibre) into the foreground. "Below Planck scale" in QOU is a categorical statement, not a metric one. The relevant geometry switches from the base M to the fibre \mathcal{S}_p, where the morphisms are knot operators.

The encounter unfolds in three moments:

  1. Approach. Two vortex tubes propagate on M and approach a common brane point p. The Reeb flow on M tracks the motion.
  2. Crossing onto the fibre. At the threshold \partial F / \partial \mathbf{c} = 0 on the colour-tube cubic, the base coordinate z hits a discriminant zero. The smooth base structure pinches. The operative morphisms transition to those of \mathcal{S}_p — the \Phi_q-piece K_S.
  3. Merging of fundamental groups. The two vortex cores become parallel strands in a single braid. Their independent fundamental groups \pi_1(\nu_1) and \pi_1(\nu_2) amalgamate into the fundamental group \pi_1(U \setminus K) of the merged knot complement. Here U is a tubular neighbourhood of p, and K is the link formed by the two strands inside it.

After moment (3), the encounter constitutes a knot-theoretic problem. The merged complement admits a hyperbolic structure. The SDP/LP machinery of Chapter 11 selects the lowest-energy link representative (SDP as thimble flow). Mostow rigidity [mostow1968] (geometric confinement) makes the resulting topology—and hence the mass—discrete.
sec:thurston-relaxation:
Thurston relaxation: SDP as a hyperbolic Newton solver

Once the two vortex cores merge inside a tubular neighbourhood U \subset M, the operative geometry is the complement U \setminus K. Thurston's hyperbolisation programme proves that, excluding a finite list of exceptions, U \setminus K admits a complete finite-volume hyperbolic structure. A triangulation into ideal tetrahedra \Delta_{z_k} and a system of gluing equations in the shape parameters z_k encode this structure.

The algebraic SDP solver of Chapter 11 is the \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}]-shadow of the hyperbolic-geometry calculation. This rests on three correspondences, which are asserted here, not established; no witness checks them:

  • Cusps from poles. The roots of the q-Pochhammer denominator \Phi_n(x; q) = \prod_{k=0}^{n-1}(1 - x q^k)^{-1} seed the Frobenius positivity constraints in the SDP.
  • Newton iteration on the gluing equations. The Newton solver for Thurston's gluing equations (e.g. SnapPy) seeds from these poles and converges to the shape parameters z_k realising the complete hyperbolic structure. The same algebraic-residue data feeds both the SDP and the gluing solver; they are different evaluations of one categorical object.
  • Steepest descent. On the Archimedean side, the residue sum becomes the Picard--Lefschetz thimble decomposition of the Seiberg--Witten action S(z) (thimble). The Gröbner--Shirshov reduction depth is expected to equal the number of ideal tetrahedra used in the triangulation (the GB--PL bijection). The SDP's complementary-slackness rank equals the number of thimble flows realising the optimum.

In short: two knots settle into the lowest-energy operator because that operator is the unique fixed point of Newton iteration on the Thurston gluing equations seeded by the q-Pochhammer poles, and that fixed point is the Archimedean realisation of the SDP optimum.

The next remark details why this functions as the "hyperbolic relaxation" picture, mapping SDP dual variables to thimble depths.
rem:radial-projection: Remark Radial projection of Bring's surface. Restrict a Briggs--Klein affine chart (Briggs--Klein chart) to the interval r\in(0,1) and project Bring's surface onto this radial coordinate. This yields a fibration over the base manifold M with trivial bundle \mathcal{S}=\mathcal{S}_0. At each r, the coordinate w_1 restricts to a circle of radius \sqrt{r} in the complex plane \mathbb{C}_{w_1}. This circle constitutes the orbit of the C_5 symmetry: the rotation w_1\mapsto\zeta w_1 moves the point along this circle without altering r.
rem:four-colourability: Remark Four-colourability of Bring's surface. By the Heawood bound, an orientable surface of genus g has chromatic number at most \lfloor(7+\sqrt{1+48g})/2\rfloor. For genus 4, this bound equals 10. Bring's surface, however, admits a proper colouring with only four colours. This low chromatic number reflects the high degree of symmetry. The S_5 automorphism group constrains the combinatorics of any cell decomposition, forcing a more efficient colouring than a generic genus-4 surface permits.
rem:four-colour-theorem: Remark The four-colour theorem and Bring's surface. The classical four-colour theorem dictates that every planar graph is four-colourable. For higher-genus surfaces, the chromatic number grows as O(\sqrt{g}) (Heawood conjecture, proved by Ringel--Youngs). That Bring's surface attains the planar bound of four at genus 4 reflects the rigidity imposed by its S_5 symmetry. In the Descartes universe, the trivial bundle \mathcal{S}=\mathcal{S}_0 (radial projection) carries no torsion. The resulting flatness of the tessellation forces the same chromatic economy as the sphere.
rem:cyclotomic-reduction:
Remark Cyclotomic reduction and C_{\mathfrak{p}} preservation. Let \mathfrak{p} be a prime (not to be confused with a point p\in M). Working over the cyclotomic ring

\begin{equation}\label{eq:cyclotomic-ring}
  \mathbb{Z}_{\zeta_{\mathfrak{p}}}
   := \mathbb{Z}[i,\zeta_{\mathfrak{p}}],
\end{equation}

where \zeta_{\mathfrak{p}}=e^{2\pi i/\mathfrak{p}} is a primitive \mathfrak{p}-th root of unity, consider the sublocus

  S_{\mathfrak{p}}
   := 
  \Sigma_4\cap\mathbb{Z}_{\zeta_{\mathfrak{p}}}^{5}.

This defines the set of points on Bring's surface whose resolvent coordinates lie in \mathbb{Z}_{\zeta_{\mathfrak{p}}}. The cyclic subgroup C_{\mathfrak{p}}\subset S_5 generated by the \mathfrak{p}-cycle preserves S_{\mathfrak{p}}. For any P\in S_{\mathfrak{p}}, the image \sigma^k(P) remains in \mathbb{Z}_{\zeta_{\mathfrak{p}}}^{5} because \sigma multiplies by \zeta_{\mathfrak{p}}^{-k} in the resolvent basis (Lagrange resolvent transform), and \zeta_{\mathfrak{p}}^{-k}\in\mathbb{Z}_{\zeta_{\mathfrak{p}}}. This arithmetic compatibility between the cyclic symmetry and the cyclotomic ring exhibits the descent of the C_5 action to finite characteristic.
sec:spectral-gauge-intro: Over the smooth curve \Sigma_4, the cyclotomic resolvent basis \{\omega_k\} carries a quaternionic \mathrm{Sp}(1) structure and a tetraplectic form on the eight-dimensional real homology H_1(\Sigma_4, \mathbb{R}) \cong \mathbb{H}^2. This section constructs the quaternionic spectral resolvents, the Reeb quaternionic twist on the Bring cone, and the Seiberg–Witten abelianisation along the exceptional divisors, and concludes by extracting the Descartes elliptic curve \mathcal{E}_q whose golden-ratio degeneration anchors the \chi = -6 condition.
